title: Lanes and the native object model
summary: The native library lane (native/NativeLibraryEmitter.cls with native/native_package_template.cpp.in, runtime headers in include/) is the main path: classes, methods, routines and the main program become C++ in one generated package whose classes are real ooRexx classes. The hybrid compiler (hybrid/compiler) emits method bodies; rules/ hold one class per statement or expression form. Built-in functions are native where ported (include/rx_bif_integration.hpp) and otherwise run by the interpreter. Native objects: strings, numbers, Array, Directory, StringTable and others are native until they cross to the interpreter (then materialised); compiled subclasses of .Array keep the array part native (InstanceState::builtin, NativeArray::answer). A message a compiled class has no method for goes through inheritedSend: builtin part, then ISA cached per class pair, then the interpreter. ::CONSTANT methods are native and hide inherited methods. Simple variables live in frames by slot; object variables in FieldFrames.
invariants: Native fast path where one exists, the interpreter otherwise; the interpreter is always present (architecture: Tom Dyer).
Compiled PROTECTED methods are not in the direct dispatch table: they go through the interpreter so the security manager is asked.
EXIT and SIGNAL in compiled bodies do not use C++ exceptions on the common path: EXIT returns when the body has no internal calls; SIGNAL is a goto to the body's _rxSignal label.
Line numbers of classes come from .local['RX2CPP.SOURCEMAP'] so SIGL and error lines match the source.

provenance.claim: Native fast paths keep interpreter results byte for byte.
